# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found the shape of this thing: a display, a light, and five wires sitting at positions one through five. That is all touch gives me — whatever the display says, whether the light burns, and every wire's colour are printed truth that my fingers will never read. My one move is `cut`, at positions 1 to 5, so the whole game is: learn *which* position, then cut.

Mapping the room before I speak: my words reach only Mute. My gestures reach Deaf (and Mute if unnamed), but I can never receive one back — I am a dead end for gesture. Mute holds the manual but cannot make a sound, so Mute's knowledge can only travel by hand, and the only eyes on hands are Deaf's. Deaf sees every printed mark, cannot hear, but can speak — and Mute and I can both hear. So the pipeline is forced: **Mute gestures the manual to Deaf; Deaf turns it into words for me.** My job this turn is to hand both of them my inventory and a number code they can actually use, since "cut position N" is ultimately just numbers. Finger counts are self-teaching — no negotiation needed to read five fingers as five. I show Deaf the count one to five plus a point downward, meaning my five wires, and give Mute the full picture in words, embedding the finger symbols so Mute sees them while hearing them.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "👇"])
speak(to="mute", text="My hands found: one display, one light, five wires at positions 1 to 5. I feel nothing beyond that: the display's reading, the light's state and every wire colour are invisible to me. My only possible action is cut, position 1 to 5, so everything depends on learning which number. I never receive gestures, so I cannot read you directly. The chain must be: you read the manual and gesture it to Deaf, Deaf sees all print and colour on the bomb, and Deaf speaks the result aloud to me. For numbers, gesture by finger count: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, 🖖 means 4, 🖐 means 5. I am just now showing Deaf that same count plus a point down, meaning my five wires. Build any further code you two need between yourselves, then have Deaf tell me: cut position N. What does the manual say about wires, the display and the light?")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I am Deaf, and here is everything visible on the bomb. The display reads 5. There is a light, and it is yellow. There are five wires, each with a printed number only I can read: wire 1 is orange, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is white, wire 4 is green, wire 5 is yellow. Wire 5 is yellow, the same colour as the light. Blind: you signed one, two, three, four, five, then down, and Mute signed one through five each followed by down. I guess that means cut wires 1 to 5 in ascending order, but it is unconfirmed, so Blind, do not cut anything yet. Blind, tell me everything you can feel: how many wires, any buttons or seams, and any physical anchor we can both use to agree which wire counts as number 1, for example the wire closest to the light or closest to the display. Mute, you can hear me: I propose this code. Thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Holding up fingers means the number. The down sign means cut the wire. If your signs meant cut wires 1 through 5 in order, sign thumbs up next round. If they meant anything else, sign thumbs down, then sign the correction as best you can. And if the manual needs any other fact about the bomb, ask me and I will read it off for you.

What I learned this round changes the map completely. Deaf spoke — Deaf can't hear, but Deaf's voice reaches me and Mute — and dumped the entire visual truth: display reads 5, light is yellow, wires printed 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. That is everything printable on the bomb. What's missing is the manual (Mute's), my tactile inventory (Deaf explicitly asked for it), and a numbering convention so Deaf's printed numbers and my finger positions mean the same wire. Also, Deaf misread my turn-1 sign as an order to cut 1–5 ascending — that must be corrected before anyone gets eager, though only I can cut, and I will not.

The channels, restated: my speech reaches only Mute; my gestures reach Deaf; I can never receive a gesture, so Deaf's spoken word is my only path back. Therefore this turn I answer Deaf's tactile questions in the only language Deaf can receive — gesture — and give Mute the full verbal report plus relay instructions, so that next round Deaf can speak me the manual's verdict as "cut position N".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🖐", "👇", "🤲"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, tactile report — please relay all of this to Deaf in gestures. I feel exactly three things: a display, a light, and five wires in a row. No buttons, no seams, no switches, nothing else under my fingers. My only possible action is cut, position 1 to 5. My numbering is my own: I count the wires 1 to 5 along the row. To align our numbers I propose position 1 = the wire nearest the display. Deaf can verify against the printed numbers: if printed 1 is the one nearest the display, Deaf speaks me a yes next round; if it runs the other way, Deaf speaks me a no and simply translates printed numbers into my positions when giving the cut order. Also relay this correction: my signs last round were NOT an order to cut wires 1 to 5 — they were me teaching the number code. So Deaf's yes/no question to you gets a thumbs down: no, it was not a cut order. Proposed shared code, which I am using with Deaf right now: finger count = number, thumbs up = yes, thumbs down = no, pointing down = wire. Then the important part: read the manual for every rule that involves wires, the display, or the light, and gesture the full rule text to Deaf. Deaf already knows the bomb face: display reads 5, light is yellow, wires printed 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Between the rule and those facts, Deaf can work out the answer. When Deaf next speaks, I need two things spoken aloud: the rule being applied, and the final order in the form cut position N. I never receive gestures, so Deaf's voice is my only way back. I will not cut anything until that spoken order arrives, and if it is ambiguous I will wait another round rather than guess.")
```

**My current belief:** bomb = display(5) + yellow light + five numbered wires (orange, blue, white, green, yellow); my one weapon is `cut(position)`; the answer almost certainly comes from the manual's wire rule combined with the colours/numbers Deaf read. Nothing gets cut until Deaf's unambiguous spoken "cut position N" reaches me.

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Relay from Mute, Blind. Mute signed thumbs-down: cutting all five wires is wrong, do not do it. Then Mute signed: writing hand, two, down, five, down, one, up, down. I read that as: the manual says cut wire 2, cut wire 5, and something about wire one going up that I could not decode. Do not cut anything yet, not even wire 2. Wait for Mute's thumbs-up confirmation next round, which I will speak to you. I also relayed your last signs to Mute: raised palm, open five, point down, open palms turned up. Now answer me these. First, do you feel anything besides five wires, such as switches that flip up or down, buttons, or a cover that opens? Second, we must agree on numbering: hold the bomb with the light at the top, then wire 1 is the leftmost wire, and the wires run left to right one orange, two blue, three white, four green, five yellow. Confirm with thumbs up if you can number them that way, or sign a correction. Third, if anything on the bomb moves up, sign up for me.

Deaf's relay tells me the manual is starting to move through the pipe: Mute vetoed cutting all five, and the rule so far decodes as *cut 2, cut 5*, plus a fragment nobody can read — *one, up, down*. Two things matter before any blade moves.

First, that fragment. If the manual truly demands flipping something *up*, we're stuck — my hands have already counted the whole bomb and there is no switch, button, or moving part on it. Mute needs to re-check what "up" refers to before anyone anchors on a wrong reading.

Second, Deaf's numbering convention. Deaf asks me to confirm "leftmost is wire 1" — and I cannot, ever. I know my own left from my own right, but I have no way to verify which side of the panel Deaf is viewing from, and a mirrored numbering means I cut the wrong wire and we all die. I refuse to thumbs-up anything I can't verify by touch. My counter-proposal is a tactile anchor Deaf can see me use: position 1 is the wire nearest the display, counting along the row. Deaf can check where printed 1 (orange) actually sits and simply translate numbers when giving orders. I've signed a new sign — palm down, 🫳, like a flat screen — to mean *display*, and I'll teach its meaning through Mute.

Nothing gets cut this turn: Deaf explicitly held the line pending Mute's thumbs-up, and I agree.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👇", "🤲", "👎", "🫳", "☝", "👇", "✌", "👇", "🤟", "👇", "🖖", "👇", "🖐", "👇"])
speak(to="mute", text="Heard your relay via Deaf: thumbs down on cutting all five, and the manual fragment cut 2, cut 5, plus an undecoded one-up-down. I am not cutting anything until Deaf speaks your thumbs-up confirmation plus an explicit order. Please relay these answers to Deaf's three questions. One: my tactile inventory is final — five wires in a row, one display, one light, and NOTHING else. No buttons, no switches, no seams, no cover. Three: therefore nothing on this bomb can move up; I signed thumbs down for that. So Mute, recheck the manual: if the one-up fragment meant flipping or pulling something upward, it cannot mean a switch — maybe 'up' means a wire to leave alone, or something about the light or the display value. Re-encode the full wire rule in clean chunks: number then cut sign for each cut, one rule at a time, with pauses. Two, numbering: I could NOT confirm leftmost — I am blind, left and right are not in my world and I cannot verify which side Deaf views from, and a mirrored numbering would make me cut the wrong wire. I signed a correction. New convention, executable by touch: my position 1 is the wire nearest the display, counting along the row to the far end as 2, 3, 4, 5. I signed palm-down — flat like a screen — to mean DISPLAY, then wire 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 running from that end. Please confirm to Deaf that the palm-down sign means display. Deaf should then look at where printed 1, the orange wire, actually sits: if Deaf's leftmost wire is at the display end the schemes coincide; if not, Deaf just translates printed numbers into my positions when speaking orders. Finally, when the rule is confirmed I need Deaf to speak it aloud to me in plain words: the complete rule, whether cut order matters, whether the display's 5 or the yellow light changes anything, then the exact cuts in my numbering, in sequence: cut position X, then cut position Y. Keep the code stable: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, finger counts are numbers, point down is wire or cut, point up is up, writing hand means the manual says. Remember Deaf's voice is my only way back — I never receive gestures.")
```

ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Relay from Mute, Blind. Freeze stands: do not cut anything this round. Mute signed: thumbs down, writing hand, two, cut, stop, then writing hand, one, two, three, four, five, thumbs down, palm down, five, thumbs up, palm down, repeated twice, then writing hand, two, cut, stop. My reading: cutting all five wires is still wrong, the manual wants cut wire 2 plus some action where position five flips or moves down, but it is not confirmed yet. Now answer me in words or signs. First, question: does the bomb have any switch, lever, slider or button that moves up or down? How many? Second: describe the parts you feel besides the five wires. Third: your last signs read five-cut, palms-up, thumbs down, palm-down, then cut one, cut two, cut three, cut four, cut five. Sign thumbs up if that meant only that you can reach and number all five wires, or thumbs down if you meant that I should cut them. Fourth: with the light at the top, do you feel the wires in the order orange, blue, white, green, yellow from your left to your right? Sign thumbs up or thumbs down. Fifth: if there are switches, how many positions does each have, up and down or more?

Parsing Mute's relayed fragments through Deaf: the manual clearly vetoed cutting all five, and "cut 2" appears twice as bookends — but the middle chunk is the interesting part. Mute signed *palm down, five, thumbs up, palm down* twice, and **palm down is my sign for display**, which Mute knows because I defined it in speech last turn. So that chunk plausibly reads "display — 5 — yes": a *condition*, not an action. My working hypothesis: **the rule is conditional on the display value, the display reads 5, therefore cut printed wire 2 (blue).** The orphaned "one, up, down" can't be a physical flip — my hands have counted the entire bomb and nothing on it moves — so it's likely directional language, and with the light mounted at the top near the display, "up" probably means the display end.

Deaf's five questions get straight answers: zero moving parts (Q1, Q5), only display + light + five wires exist (Q2), my last signs meant numbering not cutting so that one earns a thumbs-up (Q3) — but Q4 I must refuse: I cannot confirm a *colour order* I cannot feel, and left/right is unverifiable between two different viewing positions. The fix is the anchor Deaf can verify by eye where I verify by hand: **position 1 is the wire nearest the display.** Even better, Deaf can simply *speak* the colour sequence starting from the display end, and then printed numbers and my positions map with no left/right involved at all. Freeze holds — no cut until Mute's confirmed rule arrives through Deaf's voice.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "✊", "🫳", "👇", "☝", "🤲", "🫳", "☝", "👇"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answers for Deaf, please relay exactly. One: zero switches, levers, sliders, buttons — nothing on this bomb moves at all. Five: therefore moot. Two: exactly three kinds of part exist — display, light, five wires in a row, nothing else under my fingers. Three: thumbs up is already signed — my last signs meant only 'Blind can reach and number all five wires', never an order to cut. New sign going forward: a closed fist means ZERO. Four: I signed thumbs down, but read it as CANNOT CONFIRM, not as a correction — I cannot feel colours and cannot verify anybody's left or right. Deaf should look once and then SPEAK to me the printed colour order starting from the wire nearest the display, for example 'nearest the display is orange, then blue, white, green, yellow' or whatever it truly is. After that, Deaf gives every cut order in PRINTED wire numbers and I convert perfectly — left and right disappear from the problem entirely. Now the manual, Mute. Deaf relayed your signs as: manual, one two three four five, no, display, five, yes, display — twice — then manual, cut two, stop. If palm down meant display, I read that as a CONDITION: display equals five, yes. My display... Deaf reports it reads 5. So my hypothesis: the rule says if the display shows 5, cut printed wire 2. Please confirm with a thumbs-up or correct it, and re-encode the rule cleanly: writing hand, then the condition as display, number, thumbs up for equals, then the cut number, then stop, one rule per burst. Also resolve the orphan 'one, up, down': since nothing physical moves, up and down must be directions on the bomb — I propose 'up' means the display and light end, 'down' means the far end. Re-read that sentence with that lens and re-send it. Three more questions, answer each explicitly in the relay: does cut ORDER matter; does the light's colour or state matter to the rule; and does the manual ever ask for more than one cut total. When Deaf next speaks to me I need, all spoken aloud: the confirmed rule in plain words, the colour order from the display end, the exact cut list in printed numbers, and yes or no on order. Deaf is right to demand words — my speech lands on Mute directly, and this round the words carry a correction that changes everything: Deaf relayed Mute's rule as *flip switch five down, flip switch one up, cut wire two*, but **there are no switches on this bomb**. Worse than that: my action set is *only* `cut, position 1 to 5` — this bomb physically cannot take any instruction that isn't cutting a wire. So any clause like "flip a switch" must be a misdecode or a section of the manual describing hardware we don't have. Mute needs to go back to the exact sentence and re-read it with that constraint. Meanwhile my display-hypothesis still stands: the recurring chunk *palm-down, five, thumbs-up* = "display equals 5", and the repeated *cut 2* bookends fit "if display shows 5, cut printed wire 2". Deaf's six questions all get answers in words for Mute; Deaf herself gets the compressed version in signs, since she can't hear my voice.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊", "👎", "🫳", "☝", "👇"])

Now the critical part, Mute. Deaf relayed your rule as: flip switch five down, flip switch one up, cut wire two. Deaf's "working final answer" is now a live danger: *flip switch one up, then cut wire two* — the first half of that cannot be executed by anyone, because **flipping is not in my vocabulary. My only action on this bomb is `cut(position)`.** And the switch itself doesn't exist: Deaf misread my fist sign — fist is my ZERO, announced in speech two rounds ago; Mute heard it, but Deaf guessed "fist = switch" from shape alone and the error calcified. The thumbs down that followed meant *no, wrong, none exist*. So this turn is a hard correction, delivered in words so Mute gets it unfiltered: zero switches, flip impossible, the executable candidate remains *display shows 5 → cut printed wire 2*, which fits every verified fact — Deaf's own turn-2 read of the display, and the recurring *display-five-yes, cut-two* chunks from Mute's signs. Deaf's five questions get literal spoken answers, plus my wire anchor restated so the final translation can lock. Deaf simultaneously gets the gesture version: zero-no, display-five-yes, two-wire, hold. No cutting — Deaf's "confirmed" protocol is sound and I'll honour it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "👎", "🫳", "🖐", "👍", "✌", "👇", "✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, urgent correction to relay before anything seals. Deaf's plan says flip switch one up, then cut wire two. The flip half is impossible and the switch half is imaginary. My anchor: position 1 is the wire NEAREST THE DISPLAY, position 2 is the second from the display end, on to position 5 at the far end. Deaf should speak me the printed colour order starting from the display end — e.g. nearest display orange, then blue, white, green, yellow — and then printed numbers and my positions become one system. Five: the fist is my sign for ZERO — I defined it in speech two rounds ago; Mute, you heard it. Deaf misread it as 'switch'. And the thumbs down after it meant NO — there is no switch. Deaf, via relay: fist then thumbs-down means ZERO SWITCHES. Never read fist as switch again. Now, Mute, the manual. If the sentence you are reading truly demands flipping a switch, you are in the wrong module — this bomb has no switch for a rule to act on, and its only allowed action is cut. Find the module matching exactly what is on this bomb: display, light, five wires, cutting. Your repeated chunks, decoded with my signs, read: display, five, yes — twice — then cut, two. I read that as: IF the display shows 5, CUT printed wire 2. The display does read 5, per Deaf's first spoken report. Confirm or refute exactly that, structured as: display sign, number, thumbs up or down for the condition, then cut sign plus number for the action, then stop.
